posts.name: flamethrower49
posts.cooked:
So, the most obvious thing about the Scholar is his tanking capacity, which is quite notable.  But, that's not the only thing he does.  He draws a lot of cards, which are important to maintain his Elements.  He also has access to some powerful team support abilities, and a grab-bag of variably potent one-shot attacks. 

He's definitely a three difficulty.  He will always contribute with his tanking.  I can comfortably say that's not all he does, but if he doesn't get much opportunity to set up, that may be his biggest contribution to the game.  There is inherent tension between using his powers to get cards to keep his Elements, vs. using his power to heal and employ his Elements, and both can be valid choices. 

He's not immortal, sadly.  I figure he's likely to die either last, or taking sacrifice hits for others.  In some circumstances, other heroes with more consistent damage options are more likely to be able to finish the job.

posts.cooked:
Kismet fights by putting jinxes on players that often force them to change their tactics. The hero with the highest HP might start taking extra damage, or the hero that hasn't got many cards out yet might start hurting themselves every time they play a card. Her Talisman channels power from all the jinxed heros, making her increasingly more dangerous. The Talisman also lets her play extra Lucky cards and enhances her deck-stacking abilities.

BUT, if you manage to steal the Talisman, you can use its deck-controling power against her! Just be careful not to hold on to it too long or her attacks will grow more and more furious! She can't bear the thought of anyone else getting to use her powers.

Also, Inconceivable Obstruction was a card idea I thought up during playtesting, and its art and flavor text are one of my favorites.
